title: VPC network abstraction module for private deployments (subnets, NAT/IGW, endpoints, routing)
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background: The current Private deployment networking bits are split across a few older Terraform modules and ad-hoc scripts. We need a single opinionated, composable Terraform module that can be used by Private (VPC) installs and on-prem deployments to consistently provision subnets, IGW/NAT options, VPC endpoints, and route tables across regions and multiple AZs.

Goals:
- Provide an idempotent, documented Terraform module compatible with Terraform 1.5+ and AWS provider 5.x.
- Support multi-AZ public/private subnet layout, optional dedicated transit-style routing for shared services, and flexible NAT modes (managed NAT Gateway or NAT instances for cost-sensitive customers).
- Create first-class support for VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, SecretsManager, KMS, STS, CloudWatch), with a toggle-able endpoints map per environment.
- Emit clear outputs for downstream stacks: subnet IDs grouped by AZ and type, route table IDs, endpoint IDs, and the primary IGW/NAT identifiers.
- Include Terraform-level health checks: outputs/flags that can be used by health-runner to validate network connectivity and a small suite of smoke tests in CI.

Non-goals:
- This module will not replace organization-wide shared networking (Transit Gateway) patterns; it should integrate with them via optional inputs (route_table attachments) but not own TGW resources.

Intended consumers: Private deployment automation repos, on-prem install manifests, and the Dedicated infra stack when isolated networking is requested.
technical_details:
Module interface summary:
- Variables (high-level): vpc_cidr, azs, public_subnet_cidrs, private_subnet_cidrs, enable_nat_gateway (bool), nat_instance_ami (optional), enable_endpoints (map), endpoints_to_create (list), tags (map), enable_flow_logs (bool), flow_logs_config (map), create_igw (bool), route_table_mode (single|per-az|shared).
- Outputs: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, isolated_subnet_ids (opt), public_route_table_ids, private_route_table_ids, igw_id, nat_gateway_ids, endpoint_ids_map, flow_log_ids.
- Provider constraints: terraform >= 1.5, required_providers { aws = "~> 5.0" }
- Implementation notes: split into sub-modules inside the TF module: vpc-core (creates VPC, IGW, basic route tables), subnets (creates public/private/isolated subnets per AZ), nat (chooses NAT Gateway when enable_nat_gateway true; otherwise creates an HA pair of NAT instances with ASG + NAT AMI), endpoints (iterative creation with policy attachment options), routing (route propagation, optional static routes for TGW integration), flow-logs (optional, supports CloudWatch Logs and S3 sinks).
- Lifecycle and State: keep resource addressing stable across refactors by using explicit "name" tags and documented import steps. Avoid renaming resources unless major version bump.
- Security: Defaults to create endpoints for SecretsManager and KMS when enable_endpoints true. Private subnets have no IGW routes. All resources get the provided tags for cost center, org, and environment.
- Health checks from module: a "network_probe" null_resource is provisioned only in CI mode (variable ci_probe_enabled) that runs an external test runner (Terratest or remote-exec) to validate routing to endpoints and external reachability. Module also exposes a boolean output "is_configured" (derived) for quick downstream checks.
migration_plan:
Compatibility strategy:
1) Add the new module as a separate tf module and deploy to staging VPCs.
2) For existing stacks, import resources using 'terraform import' into the new module state addresses where names match. Provide an import guide script in scripts/import_vpc.sh.
3) Use feature flags to enable nat_instance vs nat_gateway without destructive changes.
4) Make all breaking changes behind a major_version input and document an upgrade guide.
5) Roll forward to production only after successful canary (see rollout plan).

Artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/VPC+Network+Module+Design (internal), Import helper: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tools/tree/main/vpc-imports
tests_and_validation:
CI validations planned:
- terraform fmt + validate + tflint run on PRs.
- Unit-like checks: terraform plan with example workspaces for small/medium/large CIDR sizes.
- Integration: Terratest suite that provisions the module in a short-lived AWS account and validates: subnets correspond to AZs, private subnet has no IGW route, NAT provides outbound internet for instances in private subnet, endpoints are present and DNS resolves, route tables attach correctly.
- Smoke scripts: python/boto3 test that creates an EC2 in each subnet class and performs curl to S3 endpoint and external web site to validate egress.
- Health checks: add a simple lambda (deployed by CI) that attempts to reach S3/ecr endpoints and reports status to the console dashboard for the canary.

CI locations: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-private/actions workflows 'vpc-module-pr-test'
rollout_and_rollback:
Rollout steps:
1) Merge module behind feature flag in infra-private repo.
2) Deploy to 'staging' account in us-west-2, run full test-suite.
3) Deploy to one customer-like canary (non-customer impacting) VPC and validate traffic.
4) Gradually apply to more customer VPCs using change-control and automation.

Rollback: Keep previous state snapshots and provide a one-button revert in the infra pipeline which re-applies the previous module version and runs the smoke tests. Any destructive changes must require manual approval and a follow-up migration ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
- Module code in repo with README and examples for small/medium/large footprints.
- Automated tests (lint, plan, terratest) pass in CI.
- Staging environment provisioned and validated by Terratest.
- Import script validated by importing one older VPC without downtime.
- Security review completed (security_review_required = true).
- Documentation: Confluence design and upgrade guide published.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Importing existing customer VPCs could cause drift or accidental replacement if addresses change.
Mitigation: Provide an 'import-check' mode that only runs 'terraform plan' with existing remote state to surface differences and requires manual approval. Use stable resource names to prevent address changes.

Risk: NAT instance option increases operational overhead.
Mitigation: Default to NAT Gateway for new installs; require explicit opt-in for NAT instance with warning in docs.

Risk: Creating too many endpoints can increase cost and complexity.
Mitigation: Provide per-endpoint toggles and sane defaults (only critical endpoints on by default).

Risk: TGW or shared-network integrations vary across customers.
Mitigation: Make TGW integration opt-in and allow external route_table attachment inputs.
